industry_landscape.market_structure: Web3 market consists of 5 layers: (1) L1/L2 execution — Ethereum ~55% TVL dominance with L2s (Arbitrum, Base, OP Mainnet, zkSync Era, StarkNet) absorbing activity at 10-100x lower fees, Solana as primary monolithic competitor with integrated UX advantage, (2) Middleware — oracles (Chainlink 70%+ market share in DeFi TVL, Pyth growing in high-frequency/perps, Redstone modular approach), bridges (Wormhole/LayerZero as infrastructure for app-specific bridges, Axelar for institutional/enterprise bridging, Hyperlane as permissionless interop), indexers (The Graph vs Subsquid vs direct RPC query), (3) DeFi — DEXs (Uniswap ~50% Ethereum volume, aggregators 1inch/0x/CowSwap capturing routing layer, Solana DEXs (Jupiter, Raydium, Orca) competing on speed/UX), lending (Aave ~65% TVL in DeFi lending, Morpho/Spark/Euler as next-gen), stablecoins (USDC $25B, USDT $90B, DAI $4.5B), (4) Application layer — wallets (Metamask ~30M MAU, Phantom, Rabby, Rainbow, coinbase wallet), identity (ENS, Lens Protocol, Farcaster as social graph), (5) Enterprise/institutional — BlackRock BUIDL fund on Ethereum, JPM Onyx, CBDC experiments (mBridge, Project Mariana, digital euro, digital yuan e-CNY, Brazil Drex)
industry_landscape.competitive_dynamics: L1 competition: Ethereum L2-centric roadmap (rollup-centric, Danksharding for DA scaling, PBS/PEPC for validator decentralization) vs Solana monolithic (single global state, hardware-scaling via Moore's law, Firedancer validator client rewrite in C for 1M+ TPS) vs modular thesis (Celestia for DA, execution rollup, settlement layer). Key battleground: interoperability winner-take-most dynamics (if all apps bridge to one hub, that hub captures value), MEV supply chain centralization (builders — 2 builders produce 80%+ of Ethereum blocks since Merge), validator centralization (Lido ~32% Ethereum stake, Coinbase ~14%, Binance ~6% — implications for censorship resistance and protocol security).
industry_landscape.business_models: Primary revenue models in Web3: (1) Protocol fees — Uniswap generated $450M+ in LP fees annually, captured by LPs not token holders (governance debate on fee switch), (2) Sequencer/validator revenue — L2 sequencers generate meaningful margin (Arbitrum One collected $50M+ in profit 2023-2024 before DA cost reduction via EIP-4844), (3) MEV extraction — Flashbots/MEV-Boost: validators earned $300M+ in MEV in 2023, (4) stablecoin float income — Tether $6.2B profit 2024 Q1 (primarily from US Treasury holdings), Circle $200M+ in 2023, (5) Wallet fee economics: Metamask swap fees (~0.875%) generated $200M+ annual revenue, (6) Infrastructure — node service (Alchemy/Infura/QuickNode), indexer (Goldsky, Subquery), API (moralis, covalent), all with SaaS-like recurring revenue at $0.5-1B+ valuation multiples.

technology_architecture.l1_design_spectrum: Blockchain design is fundamentally a trilemma between decentralization, security, and scalability. L1 design decisions: (1) Execution environment choice — EVM (largest developer ecosystem, tooling maturity, composability) vs alt-VM (SVM — parallel execution, Move — resource-oriented programming, CosmWasm — sandboxed with interchain accounts) vs custom VM (zkVM — RISC-V/MIPS instruction set, Cairo VM — algebraic intermediate representation). (2) Consensus mechanism — single-slot finality (Tendermint, HotStuff derivatives) vs probabilistic finality (longest chain, GHOST) vs hybrid (Gasper — LMD-GHOST + Casper FFG, 2-epoch finality). (3) Data availability — on-chain (monolithic) vs off-chain (validium/committee) vs DAS (data availability sampling with erasure coding), DA throughput comparison (Ethereum calldata ~80KB/slot, Celestia blobs ~2MB/block, EigenDA 10MB/s with erasure coding). (4) State model — accounts (Ethereum) vs UTXO (Bitcoin, Cardano) vs hybrid (EUTXO — Ergo, object-based — Sui), each with different parallelism and privacy trade-offs.
technology_architecture.l2_rollup_taxonomy: Rollup types: (1) Optimistic rollups — 7-day fraud proof window (Arbitrum, OP Mainnet, Base), permissionless validation via interactive bisection protocol, cost structure: L1 calldata cost (reduced 10x post-EIP-4844) + L2 compute, (2) ZK-rollups — instant finality via validity proofs (zkSync Era, StarkNet, Polygon zkEVM, Scroll, Linea), cost structure: proof generation (amortized over batch, ~$0.001-0.01/tx at scale) + proof verification on L1 (~500k gas per batch) + L1 blob/calldata, (3) Sovereign rollups — use L1 for DA only, do own settlement (e.g., rollup using Celestia for DA + sovereign execution, no L1 bridge — no L1 security for bridging). Rollup stages framework (Vitalik): Stage 0 (full training wheels — multisig can override), Stage 1 (limited training wheels — security council with threshold, fraud proof system active), Stage 2 (no training wheels — fully permissionless, code is law). Most L2s are still Stage 0 or 1.
technology_architecture.defi_architecture_patterns: DeFi composition patterns: (1) Hub-and-spoke — central liquidity hub (e.g., Balancer pool) with aggregator spokes, (2) Modular money legos — each protocol does one thing well, composed via multicall/vaults (Yearn, Instadapp), (3) Monolithic protocols — single protocol handles multiple functions (MakerDAO — stablecoin + lending + RWA), (4) Intents-based — user signs intent, solver fills optimally (CowSwap, UniswapX, 1inch Fusion). Key architecture decisions: oracle model (push vs pull, number of sources, aggregation method, heartbeat interval, deviation threshold, circuit breaker — each affects security/latency/cost triangle), upgradeability pattern (UUPS vs Transparent proxy vs Beacon proxy vs Diamond pattern vs immutable — trade-off between bug-fix-ability and trust/censorship resistance), access control (Role-based vs ownership-based vs timelock + governance vs immutable — graduated decentralization path).

strategic_frameworks.why_web3_decision_framework: Decision tree: Does this product REQUIRE: (1) Censorship resistance — no single party can block transactions? (2) Trustless coordination — parties who don't trust each other must coordinate? (3) Programmable value — money needs code-level composability? (4) User sovereignty — users must control their own assets/identity/data? If none apply → Web3 is probably the wrong solution. If 1-2 apply → consider hybrid (Web2 UX + Web3 settlement). If 3-4 apply → full Web3 is warranted.
strategic_frameworks.tokenomics_design: Framework steps: (1) Define value proposition — what scarcity/coordination/ incentive problem does the token solve that existing solutions don't? (2) Identify value capture — where in the protocol does value flow? (fees, MEV, governance, data, network effects), (3) Map stakeholder incentives — who benefits, who pays, who has power? Does any stakeholder have incentive to attack the system? (4) Design supply mechanics — initial distribution (fairness vs growth trade-off), emission schedule (supply predictability vs adaptability), sinks (where does value accrue to token holders?), (5) Simulate under stress — model token price -90%, usage -95%, major competitor emerges, regulatory hostile jurisdiction — does the system survive? (6) Iterate with data — ship minimal viable tokenomics, measure actual behavior (not modeled), adjust parameters that are governance-controlled. Never launch with 'tokenomics will be decided later by DAO' — this is a rug pull red flag.
strategic_frameworks.decentralization_maturity: Framework: (1) Technical decentralization — Stage 0 (multisig), Stage 1 (security council + timelock + fraud proofs), Stage 2 (immutable, permissionless). (2) Economic decentralization — single entity controls >50% supply → oligopoly (2-5 entities) → widely distributed (no entity >5%). (3) Governance decentralization — single entity controls decisions → core team retains veto → token holder governance with high participation → liquid democracy with delegation. (4) Infrastructure decentralization — single cloud provider → multi-cloud → multi-region → geo-distributed validators with diverse clients. Each project should publish their current stage and roadmap for each dimension.
strategic_frameworks.regulatory_arbitrage: Framework for jurisdiction selection: (1) Entity formation — Switzerland for non-profit/foundation (regulatory clarity, banking access), Cayman/BVI for token issuer (tax neutrality, common law, institutional investor familiarity), UAE (ADGM/DIFC) for operational hub, US (Wyoming) for domestic-facing DAO. (2) Token offering — exclude US persons (Reg S offering offshore + Reg D 506(c) for accredited US investors only — NEVER general solicitation to US retail). (3) Exchange listing — top-tier (Binance, Coinbase) require 12+ months of legal cleanup before even discussing, mid-tier (Bybit, OKX, Kraken, KuCoin) 6-12 months, DEX-first then CEX as regulatory posture clarifies. (4) Ongoing compliance — maintain legal analysis memos updated quarterly (regulations change), OFAC screening integrated at smart contract level (or frontend — debate), AML/KYC for fiat on/off-ramps only (not DeFi protocol itself if truly decentralized — but 'truly decentralized' is actively contested).
